name: Muséum d'histoire naturelle de Port-Louis
pitch: Musée gratuit du centre de Port-Louis : quatre galeries d'histoire naturelle, dont un squelette de dodo issu d'un seul oiseau.
description_md: Le Natural History Museum occupe le rez-de-chaussée du Mauritius Institute Building, face au Jardin de la Compagnie, au centre de Port-Louis. Le bâtiment, construit entre 1880 et 1884, est classé patrimoine national. D'après le Mauritius Museums Council, c'est le plus ancien musée de Maurice. Ses quatre galeries permanentes retracent 500 ans d'histoire naturelle de l'île : oiseaux, mammifères et reptiles, vie marine, géologie et insectes, et une galerie consacrée au dodo.
why_go_md: L'entrée est gratuite. La galerie du dodo montre une maquette de l'oiseau et un squelette recueilli en 1900 dont tous les os proviennent du même individu, ce que le musée présente comme unique.

sources.title: Natural History Museum – Historical Background – Mauritius Museums Council
sources.evidence: The Natural History Museum is located on the ground floor of the Mauritius Institute Building, right in front of the “Jardin de la Compagnie”, in the heart of the City of Port Louis. The Mauritius Institute Building, constructed between 1880 and 1884, is listed as a National Heritage.

sources.title: Natural History Museum – Historical Background – Mauritius Museums Council
sources.evidence: The Natural History Museum is the oldest museum of Mauritius and amongst the oldest in southern Africa.

sources.title: Natural History Museum – About The Museum – Mauritius Museums Council
sources.evidence: The Natural History Museum, through its four permanent galleries, presents the past 500 years of the natural history of Mauritius. The first gallery exhibits mammals, reptiles and mostly birds.

sources.title: Natural History Museum – About The Museum – Mauritius Museums Council
sources.evidence: The second gallery is wholly dedicated to marine life [...] The third gallery has sections on geology, corals, shrimps, insects, turtles and local woods. [...] An insectarium showing almost complete collection of butterflies

sources.title: Natural History Museum – About The Museum – Mauritius Museums Council
sources.evidence: A model of the Dodo, the centrepiece of the museum, is displayed in this gallery. The skeleton of the Dodo, collected by E. Thirioux, a barber, in 1900, is unique in the sense that all the bones come from one individual bird.
